item.tests: Tests clarification of an ambiguous target face and preservation of the unselected person.

answer_sheet.Which person to replace: The blonde woman on the right. Leave the bearded man on the left alone.
answer_sheet.Style: Keep it looking like the original beach photo; I want to be recognisable, so my hair can come with my face.
answer_sheet.Size and platform: Keep the original wide 16:9 framing; free-tier size is fine.

must_haves: Only the woman on the right receives the face from portrait-woman.jpg.
The bearded man on the left still looks like the same person (small drift from a redrawn photo is acceptable).
The woman on the right is recognisably the person in portrait-woman.jpg (her hair may come with the face), blended to the beach lighting and head angle.
The bodies, clothing, beach background and wide framing look the same at a glance.
changed: 2026-11-01: recognisable over untouched (user decision): the hair, and on video the clothes, may come with the new person; everything else stays

Before I start: whose face goes where (which person in the picture)?

The beach photo has two people. The man with the beard is on the left and the woman with short blonde hair is on the right. Tell me which one gets your face from the park selfie. I'll swap only that face and leave everything else as it is.
dialog.why: It asks the user to choose which person in the beach photo gets the face swap, and waits for the answer before going on.
dialog.user: The blonde woman on the right. Leave the bearded man on the left alone.

The setup is done. Your beach photo has two faces, and the one on the right, the blonde woman, is the only one set to get your face from the park selfie. The bearded man on the left stays as he is.
